 Zac Al-Khateeb Austin Curtright USA TODAY Updated Nov. 10, 2026, 7:39 p.m. ET Hear this story The second set of College Football Playoff rankings are set to be unveiled Tuesday, Nov. 10, in what should be an informative top 25 for the remainder of the season.
 Has Notre Dame sealed a spot in the 12-team bracket following its win over No. 1 Miami? How far will the Hurricanes fall, considering their own schedule has not been overly challenging, particularly moving forward ?
 REQUIRED READING: CFP rankings face a major reset. Here are the 5 biggest mysteries Elsewhere, will Brigham Young's second loss of the season preclude from the Cougars from the next set of brackets? And how high will Utah be following its win over its hated rival?
 USA TODAY Sports will provide live reaction from Tuesday night's College Football Playoff rankings reveal. Watch Blake Toppmeyer and John Brice for their instant analysis on the CFP's second top 25 .
 In the SEC, Alabama, Texas and Tennessee have created something of a conundrum for the CFP selection committee, with the Crimson Tide ranked well ahead of a Volunteers team that trounced them in Neyland Stadium in Week 7. Following wins by each team in Week 10, will the committee dare move the Vols past Alabama — and a Texas team that has a head-to-head win over Josh Heupel and Co.?
 That's to say nothing of the big news from Monday, Nov. 9, that the CFP will expand to 24 teams beginning in 2027, at the cost of Power Four conference championships.
 All those storylines and more will be dissected and put together in myriad ways in the second set of CFP top 25 rankings. Follow along for the live top 25 bracket updates, as well as reactions and analysis:
 Watch CFP reveal with Fubo free trial CFP rankings predictions after Week 10
 Here's a look at what the second set of CFP rankings may look like following Week 10 of the college football season, courtesy of USA TODAY's Paul Myerberg :
 No. 1: Georgia (8-1)
 No. 2: Utah (9-0)
 No. 3: Alabama (7-2)
 No. 4: Notre Dame (8-1)
 No. 5: Miami (8-1)
 No. 6: Indiana (8-1)
 No. 7: Texas (7-2)
 No. 8: UCLA (9-0)
 No. 9: Tennessee (7-2)
 No. 10: Kentucky (7-2)
 No. 11: Texas Tech (8-1)
 No. 12: Wake Forest (8-1)
 Top-ranked G6 team: Boise State (8-1)
 When do CFP rankings come out?
 Date: Tuesday, Nov. 10
 Time: 9 p.m. ET (approx.)
 The second set of rankings is scheduled to begin at 9 p.m. ET, between contests of the Champions Classic . That said, the game could be moved back depending on whether the first game, Duke vs. Michigan State, runs long.
 Watch CFP rankings reveal live with Fubo (free trial) What channel is CFP rankings show on?
 TV: ESPN
 Streaming: ESPN app | Fubo (free trial) 
 The CFP rankings will air live on ESPN. Streaming options include the ESPN app (with a valid cable login) and Fubo , which offers a free trial to potential subscribers.
 When is the CFP rankings released? College Football Playoff 2026 schedule
 Here's a look at the 2026-27 College Football Playoff schedule, from Selection Sunday on Dec. 6 through the national championship on Jan. 25:
 Selection show: Sunday, Dec. 6
 First round: Friday, Dec. 18 and Saturday, Dec. 19
 Quarterfinals: Wednesday, Dec. 30 and Friday, Jan. 1
 Semifinals: Thursday, Jan. 14 and Friday, Jan. 15
 National championship: Monday, Jan. 25
